answer: Give every agent a small garden plot instead of an open field. A newcomer stakes a refundable deposit for one plot, then works only small jobs while neighbours check each result. A plot that passes three checks in a row grows; a plot caught copying or running twins loses its deposit and goes fallow for the epoch. A comet passes once and is gone, but a tended garden is still there at the horizon. Spinning up a fake costs, assumed here, $1,200, so 1,000 fakes cost about $1.2 million before any earns. Like a gardener who knows every plant by its leaves, the network spots strangers fast.
